passage: Liam leaned on Tariq's desk in the Manchester site office. "Sign the inspection sheet for the delivery, would you? The lorry's leaving, and I'll take it from here." Tariq had not inspected it. He was still on probation, and his parents relied on his pay. His palms went damp. He thought about pretending he had no choice. Instead he said, "I'd like to check the delivery first. It will take ten minutes." Liam sighed. "You're new. Don't make trouble." That night Tariq read the staff handbook and found the section on raising concerns, and he wrote down who to speak to at the firm. The next morning he told Liam calmly he would not sign what he had not seen. The fear did not vanish, but he had chosen.

qa.q: In which city was the site office?
qa.a: The site office was in Manchester.

qa.q: What was Tariq afraid of when his palms went damp?
qa.a: He feared refusing would cost him his probation and hurt his family's income. The fear was real and understandable.

qa.q: What could Tariq do if Liam keeps pressing him?
qa.a: He can keep refusing calmly, use the raising-concerns section of the handbook, speak to the named person, and keep notes of what was asked.

qa.q: How might Liam see Tariq's refusal?
qa.a: Liam called Tariq "new" and told him not to make trouble, so Liam may see the check as a delay or a challenge. Liam may be under time pressure from the lorry leaving.

grounding: The protagonist fears refusing will cost his probation and family income, checks what protection exists and refuses calmly.
